# iliad-135 review (Iliad 21.298–399), pass 1

Reviewer pass 1 over `units.json` only. `gloss.json` was not read or touched (the glosser was writing it; it belongs to pass 2). `t` untouched, checked by script (every edit asserted an exact single match; the `t` list is compared before the write). File format preserved. Structure checked by script: every `l` has the line division of `t`, every `ln` is the line the unit begins in, no newline in any `i`, ¶ units carry `p` (298, 324, 342, 361, 377, 381, 383), the six speeches have “ on the first unit, ” on the last (308–322, 331–341, 357–360, 369–376, 379–380, 394–399) and `mark` on the first unit of each; 298 follows the closing ” of iliad-134's last unit (the speech of Poseidon and Athena ends at 297).

Findings applied: 24 (major 1, moderate 14, minor 9). Findings refused or checked and left: 11.

## Considered and refused (or left)

1. **ἀλέξω “keep off” / “keep away” (374).** The table is not consistent: 9.251 (ἀλεξήσεις) gives “ward off” and lists “keep away” as avoided; 13.475 and 21.138 reserve “ward off” for ἀμύνω. The drafter followed the later rows and said so in new-renderings.md. Left; the caller may wish to decide.
2. **mark “Scamander speaks”** (308, 357, 369) against iliad-134's “The river speaks” for the same speaker. A heading, not a rendering; the name is given in the part (305). Left.
3. **ἔχραε “aorist of χράω” (369).** Imperfect or aorist cannot be told from the form; the label is defensible. Left.
4. **κατ’ αὐτόν (344), “likeliest reading Achilles”.** The note is already hedged. Left.
5. **ἐν … ἵει (338).** Note says the wording is open; `i` picks one reading, `l` keeps both. Within the rules. Left.
6. **“tender-fed pig” against the note's “σίαλος a fattened pig” (363).** The note defines the noun; `l`/`i` keep ἁπαλο- “tender”. Not a contradiction. Left.
7. **ζεῖ “boils” in `l`, “seethes” in `i` (362).** `i` may vary. Left.
8. **ἴσχεν “did not hold” (`l`) / “could not hold” (`i`) (303); ἀειρόμενον “rising” (`l`) / “rising high” (`i`) (327).** Inside the freedom of `i`. Left.
9. **λωτός “lotus”, note “a fodder plant, not the lotus-fruit” (351).** Matches the house row 2.776 (“lotus” with that note). Left.
10. **Formulas checked against the table and found right:** ποταμὸς βαθυδίνης, διιπετέος ποταμοῖο, ἀκάματον πῦρ, ὀπωρινὸς Βορέης, ἀργεστᾶο Νότοιο, πορφύρεον κῦμα “surging”, εὐρὺ ῥέων “wide-flowing”, δινήεις “eddying”, ἀϋτμή “blast”, τείρω “worn down”, ἐκπέρσει “sack”, ἀρήϊοι υἷες Ἀχαιῶν, μαλερῷ πυρί “devouring fire”, ἀγακλεές, κέκλετ’ ἀΰσας, ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζεν, πολὺς ὀρυμαγδός “din”, λέβης “cauldron”, δαϊκταμένων αἰζηῶν (21.146, cited in the note), the Odyssey-shared προσεφώνεεν ὃν φίλον υἱόν.
11. **Quotation marks and `mark`s, ¶ flags, line numbers, cross-references (332/337, 311, 330, 342, 345, 354, 371, 309, last-part Asteropaeus fish).** All checked true; no change.

The “aor. 2 sg.” of ἔδαψας, ὦσας is the second person of a first aorist; the glossary writes “aor. 2” only for the second aorist, so the notation is ambiguous but is the existing house style; left.
